note: Pilot-level help for lagging brain motor contracts (haltere.liftoff.fast_race_cue.MotorAssistConfig; visual_brain --motor-assist on|off|DECLARATION, off by default, recorded in the flight-log sidecar under pilot_assistance.motor_assist and motor_assist_declaration; CSV columns assist_pilot_vx/vy/vz, assist_horizontal, assist_vertical, assist_source, assist_plan, assist_wall_ahead only when on). Version 2 of the rule; version 1 (configs/pilot/motor_assist_v1.json, sha256 eefb4a42...) is kept for provenance and replays and refused by the runner. Declared per motor contract, never per course or per brain: the entry of the brain contract (fast_velocity_brain_v1: fast-brain-08, brain-09b, fast-brain-10b, fast-brain-11-b-cw13) applies to every brain of that contract; the fast PD contract has no entry and flies bit-identically with the flag on. Generic and causal: it reads the measured velocity, the pilot's own rule states (its final request and its request before the looming governor, the checkpoint marker's state and bearing, turn-first, the governor's cap, samples and stand-off, the ceiling guard's overhead bound) and nothing of the course: no geometry, route, logged position or per-course value. Version 2 answers the round-4b review of version 1 (its assisted request stepped by up to 4.5 m/s per tick, and its stopping source asked brains for 0.01-0.4 m/s at the Minus Two first arch, before pillar A and at the 90-degree arch) and the round-4b live hairpin failure minus-brain11cw13-r4b-noassist-01 (the looming TTC fell from ~1 s to 0.2 s while the governor stayed armed and its cap dropped only ~0.5 s before the wall). The live logs named here were read to design the rule: any replay of them is development evidence. The values were chosen on development sets only (development_results), never on the gate sets of configs/pilot/motor_assist_gates.json version 2, frozen with this declaration before any gate run. The hash covers everything except frozen/frozen_at/sha256; a change needs a new version and a new freeze. Surrogate results and open-loop replays are development evidence, never flight evidence.
rule: Version 1's two parts are unchanged in form (cap tracking of the binding caps: request, governor, turn_first, stopping; sag compensation), with version 2's changes: (a) Slew: the assist's change of the request (assisted - the pilot's own) moves per tick by at most slew x dt, as a horizontal vector and vertically each (the clearance brake bounds its own steps the same way), on onsets and releases. (b) Wall ahead: the stopping source (the motor's stopping model on the latest wall sample's dead-reckoned distance) acts only while a wall-ahead condition holds: the checkpoint marker clamped at a side edge (state side), its bearing wall_ahead_deg or more off the heading (a marker in view or clamped at the bottom/top edge), the marker lost (coast, search), a turn-first episode or its side guard, or (wall_ahead_standoff) the governor's stand-off. It keeps the latest wall sample for stop_memory_s after its last confirmation unless a newer looming sample with evidence is not a wall sample. (c) Approach: outside a wall-ahead condition the same confirmed wall samples feed the approach source, the same stopping model with its bound never below floor_speed, and not while the pilot's own vertical request before the looming governor and the vertical guard exceeds approach_climb_max (rising ground is the vertical guard's). The two share one cap-tracking extra reduction. (d) standoff_tracking false: no cap tracking of the governor's cap while it holds a stand-off (the governor itself holds the drone at or below its stand-off speed there).

parameter_notes.unchanged: cap_deadband, cap_gain, cap_max, cap_reverse, cap_rise, cap_fall, stop_ttc_s, stop_confirm, stop_window_s, stop_latency_s, stop_deceleration, stop_margin_m and every sag parameter are version 1's (see motor_assist_v1.json parameter_notes): the stopping model is the wall pilot's measured model of this contract (latency 0.3 s, 3.5 m/s^2, margin 0.5 m)
parameter_notes.slew: 15 m/s^2 is the TTC clearance governor's brake_slew, the rate at which the pilot's own clearance brake moves the request: the motor's request now changes per 10 ms tick by at most the pilot's own change plus 0.15 m/s horizontally and 0.15 m/s vertically. The round-4b review measured version 1's assisted request stepping by 3.0-4.5 m/s per tick on the Minus Two brain logs (the pilot's own at most 0.23-0.31). Development: with the slew the hairpins lost nothing against version 1 (v2any: version 1 + slew, dev17 clean 8 and 10 of 12 for fast-brain-11-b-cw13 and fast-brain-10b, as version 1)
parameter_notes.wall_ahead: wall_ahead_deg 50 is turn-first's engage_deg. The states and conditions are turn-first's triggers (TurnFirstConfig): there the next checkpoint does not lie through the surface ahead. The first arch, pillar A and the 90-degree arch of Minus Two are flown toward a marker in view, so version 2 never plans a stop there (open-loop replays of the development logs: lowest plan before x = 73 m 2.5 m/s; version 1's stopping source asked 0.01-0.4 m/s at those places)
parameter_notes.wall_ahead_standoff: false: the governor's stand-off was also a trigger in development (the task named it). It changed no development hairpin (dev17 8/9/10 with and without, fast-brain-11-b-cw13/10b/09b) but added planned stops behind the governor's own stand-offs at arches (minus-brain11cw13-r4b-noassist-01 x 22.8-23.7, after the first arch: stopping 2.44 -> 0.81 s/min without it). During a stand-off the governor holds the request at or below 2 m/s along its ray by itself; turn-first keeps its own stand-off condition
parameter_notes.standoff_tracking: false: no cap tracking of the governor's cap during its stand-off. With it, brain-09b touched the floor in 3 of 12 of version 1's gate hairpins (seed 23, development for version 2) after long governor-source tracking behind a stand-off cap (the slow brain asked to back away pitched back and sank); without it 0 (clean 7 -> 8; dev17 10 -> 11, floor 1 -> 0)
parameter_notes.stop_memory_s: 1 s (turn-first's brake_recent_s): past the arch at the Minus hairpin the live samples read no evidence within ~2 m of the wall (minus-brain11cw13-r4b-noassist-01 from 23.24 s; minus-brain09b-r4-01 from 22.52 s), so the version-1 condition (two samples in 0.25 s, the newest one of them) released the bound just when a wall-ahead condition began
parameter_notes.floor_speed: 2.5 m/s: the brain contract's stopping model stops from 2.5 m/s within 0.3 x 2.5 + 2.5^2 / 7 + 0.5 = 2.14 m, the room behind a gate arch before a wall (the Minus Two hairpin arch stands about 2.8 m before its wall; the harness hairpins 2.1-3.0 m), and it stays above the governor's min_speed 2 m/s. Development: 2.5, 3.0 and 3.5 m/s gave the same pass-through results (the governor's own stand-off decides them, see risks); 3.0 gave one clean hairpin fewer for fast-brain-11-b-cw13 (dev17 7 against 8)
parameter_notes.approach_climb_max: 0.3 m/s on the pilot's vertical request before the governor and the vertical guard: on the clean Straw Bale brain-08 laps the approach otherwise acted 1.7-3.3 s per minute, mostly at the uphill rings while the pilot followed the slope up (the version-1 quiet failure); with it 0.44-1.09 s per minute, and the hairpins lost nothing (dev17 8/8/10 against 8/9/10). The request after the guard is not used: at the minus-brain10b-r4-02 hairpin the vertical guard climbed 1 m/s on the wall's below-path samples, and that climb would have switched the approach off exactly there

development_results.scope: All development, none of it a gate set of version 2: the hairpin sets dev17 (turn 20/60/90 deg x arch 7/11 m x wall 2.1/2.6 m, sim seed 17; version 1's development set) and g23 (45/75/105 x 8/13 x 2.3/3.0, seed 23; version 1's gate set, now seen), the pass-through arch set pt17 (new: turn 0/45/90 deg x see-through 1/2 m, seed 17), all under the m4b pilot (deployed_pilot_kwargs, lag turn v2, gap pilot v5, wall pilot v5, vertical guard v4, descent view v2 with contact support); open-loop replays of the Minus Two brain logs minus-brain08-gapon-01/-02, -gapshadow-01, -loom-01, -vg-01, minus-brain09b-vg-01, minus-brain09b-r4-01, minus-brain10b-r4-02, minus-brain11cw13-r4b-noassist-01, and the Straw Bale and Pine Valley laps straw-brain08-01/-02/-03/-04/-06, pine-brain08-01, pine-brain08-loom-01 (session scratchpad m5/brake: dev_replay.py, harness_dev.py, rep4/, hp3/)
development_results.hairpin_clean: clean passes of 12 (fast-brain-11-b-cw13 / fast-brain-10b / brain-09b): baseline (no assist) 0/0/0 on both sets; version 1 dev17 8/10/11, g23 7/7/9; this version dev17 9/8/11, g23 6/7/8 (floor contacts 0 on both; version 1 g23 0, dev17 09b 1); without the approach source (the stopping source only under wall-ahead conditions) dev17 0/0/8, g23 5/2/4
development_results.pass_through: pt17 (report): lowest speed from 1.5 s before to 0.5 s after the arch pass, baseline 4.05-4.55 m/s; version 1 0.10-0.97; this version 0.42-1.04 m/s (fast-brain-11-b-cw13, fast-brain-10b): the approach slows the brain to 2.5-3 m/s, then the TTC governor's own stand-off (target 0.7 x closing speed <= 2 m/s) holds the pilot's request at about 1 m/s for 2 s; the fast PD without any assist also dips to 0.22-2.75 m/s in this scenario
development_results.replays_minus: planned near-stops before the hairpin (x < 73 m): version 1 the stopping bound at 0.0-0.4 m/s at the first arch (x 15-19), before pillar A (x 44-47) and at the 90-degree arch (x 67-70) on every brain log; this version none (lowest plan 2.5 m/s). Hairpin: 1.0 s before the minus-brain11cw13-r4b-noassist-01 impact the motor would be asked 3.53 m/s (the pilot 5.86; the governor's cap was still 7.31 there), 0.5 s before 1.13 (3.66); minus-brain10b-r4-02 2.74 (4.25) and 1.31 (3.85). Per-tick change of the assist: at most 15.0 m/s^2 horizontally and 15.0 vertically (version 1: 207-604 m/s^2)
development_results.replays_straw: clean brain-08 laps: stopping source 0.02-0.12 s per minute, approach 0.44-1.09 s per minute (version 1's stopping 1.8-3.3); request travel removed by the stopping model 0.2-0.6% of the pilot's own, by every source 1.3-2.7%

not_included.request_floor: a floor on every cap-tracking source outside wall-ahead conditions (the first design): it stopped cap tracking from pushing a lagging brain below the approach bound, and the brains reached the arch too fast (dev17 clean 6/6/11 against 9/8/11)
not_included.wall_ray: wall-ahead also when the checkpoint's bearing is 30 or 45 deg off the latest wall sample's ray: hairpins within one pass of 12 either way, and it planned a stop after the 90-degree arch on minus-brain09b-vg-01 (x 72)
not_included.lower_window: an approach sample explained by the lower window (ttc_lower <= ttc) counted as terrain: no effect beyond approach_climb_max on the Straw laps
not_included.gap_cue_wall: the gap cue's r_peak (a wall filling the view reads ~1): at the Minus arches 57-74% of the approach ticks read below 1.35 too; no separation from the hairpins
not_included.governor_standoff: the pass-through crawl is the TTC governor's stand-off (wall pilot, shared with the fast PD): the assist only lowers the pilot's request and cannot remove it; see the risks

risks: Not flight evidence. (1) Pass-through arches: slowing a brain toward an arch whose looming surface stays in view to within 1-2 m makes the TTC governor's own stand-off hold the request near 1 m/s for about 2 s in the surrogate (the live minus-brain11cw13-r4b-noassist-01 had such a crawl at x 22-26 without any assist); a stand-off only under wall-ahead conditions would be a wall-pilot change. (2) Hairpins: the brain reaches the arch at 2.5-3 m/s and must stop in the room behind it; the harness's hairpins pass 6-11 of 12, not 12. (3) Straw Bale: the approach still acts 0.4-1.1 s per minute at two level places per lap (x 65 y 2, x 77 y 14 on the brain-08 laps). (4) Ceiling: the contact-support false fire (2 of 12 harness drones) is unchanged.

previous_versions.scored: 12 of 16 gates (0c3f56c); not flown: the round-4b review found its request steps and near-stops at arches
